records.title: Pasteur vaccine program: anthrax public trial, attenuation practice and rabies treatment
records.sourceNativeSummary: Pasteur's laboratory moved from attenuated animal vaccines to highly visible anthrax and rabies interventions. Public trials made efficacy claims legible beyond the laboratory, while rabies treatment also required an institute/distribution system because repeated doses, timing and access mattered.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A celebrated public trial is stronger than a private claim but not identical to all-world efficacy/safety. Early rabies vaccine could itself cause serious adverse effects; availability and delivery remained separate from the biological principle.

sources.supports: attenuation, anthrax trial and rabies program
1885 treatment, multi-dose delivery and institute/access complements

records.title: Yellow-fever transmission experiments to Panama vector-control system
records.sourceNativeSummary: Reed's commission built on Finlay's mosquito hypothesis to establish Aedes transmission through controlled exposure and exclusion evidence; Gorgas then converted that causal result into an integrated Panama control system of drainage, larvicides, screening and enforcement.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Identifying the vector did not automatically remove disease. Panama required sustained operational infrastructure; later vector-control history also shows apparent eradication success can decay when institutional support disappears.

sources.supports: Reed/Finlay lineage and Gorgas integrated Panama measures/outcomes
1901 vector identification and Panama source reduction/oiling/fumigation

records.title: Radioactivity: Becquerel anomaly, Curie isolation and Rutherford–Soddy transformation
records.sourceNativeSummary: Becquerel's covered photographic plate unexpectedly showed uranium emissions independent of sunlight; Curie turned the anomaly into quantitative ionization measurements and laborious chemical isolation of polonium/radium; Rutherford and Soddy then modeled radioactive decay as transformation between elements.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The initial photographic anomaly did not contain the later element/transmutation ontology. Repeated chemical and decay evidence changed the meaning of the phenomenon over years, while early medical/commercial radium enthusiasm outran hazard knowledge.

sources.supports: Becquerel covered photographic plate and 1902–03 decay/transmutation

records.title: Electron and nuclear atom: cathode rays, scattering and charge measurement
records.sourceNativeSummary: Thomson's cathode-ray experiments inferred a universal negatively charged constituent; Geiger–Marsden scattering later produced rare large deflections incompatible with diffuse-charge models and Rutherford proposed a compact nucleus; Millikan's oil-drop measurements independently constrained elementary charge.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Each experiment measured a different representation of atomic structure. Thomson's useful model was later narrowed rather than rendered scientifically worthless; Rutherford's nucleus did not yet specify the later quantum atom.

sources.supports: Thomson electron and changing element ontology

records.title: Planck and Einstein light quanta against classical radiation theory
records.sourceNativeSummary: Planck introduced energy quanta to fit black-body radiation around 1900; Einstein in 1905 applied a stronger light-quantum interpretation to the photoelectric effect. The mathematical fix and the later ontology were not identical steps.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A formula's empirical success does not automatically license every interpretation of it. Classical wave theory remained powerful and light quanta faced substantial resistance; later quantum theory preserved and transformed both wave and particle descriptions.

sources.supports: 1900 Planck quanta and 1905 Einstein photoelectric work

records.title: Brownian-motion quantitative evidence for atoms/molecules
records.sourceNativeSummary: Einstein's 1905 statistical theory turned irregular visible particle motion into quantitative predictions about invisible molecular impacts; Perrin's 1908 experiments varied particles/liquids and repeatedly estimated Avogadro-scale quantities, helping settle a dispute over whether atoms were physically real.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Observed Brownian motion predated the molecular explanation by decades. A visible random signal did not itself identify the cause; theory became persuasive because independent quantitative predictions generalized across materials and measurements.

sources.supports: Perrin methods, varied conditions and Avogadro estimates

records.title: Noble gases force periodic-table representation change
records.sourceNativeSummary: A density anomaly in atmospheric nitrogen led Rayleigh/Ramsay toward argon; Ramsay then identified additional inert gases. The discoveries did not simply add entries to Mendeleev's table—they required a new group whose chemical inertness did not fit the old layout naturally.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A powerful representation can be correct/productive yet incomplete. Adding a new group is evidence for representation revision under anomaly, not evidence that the earlier periodic framework had no value.

sources.supports: later physical discoveries forcing periodic representation change
